properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued October 16 at 6:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...The South Coast AQMD has issued an air quality alert due to
increased fine particle pollution from wildfire smoke.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...in the areas of San Clemente, Dana Point, San Juan
Capistrano, and Laguna Niguel. Levels of particle pollution can
vary by time and location depending on fire activity and local
weather conditions.

* WHEN...from 4 PM Friday to 10 AM Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Particles in wildfire smoke can get deep into the lungs
and cause serious health problems such as heart attacks, strokes,
asthma attacks, and difficulty breathing. Everyone can be affected,
but people with lung or heart disease, older adults, people who are
pregnant, children, and those who spend a lot of time outdoors are
at greater risk.
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, if you smell or see smoke:

* Remain indoors with windows and doors closed
* Avoid intense outdoor physical activity
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* If you must be outdoors, keep the time brief and wear a well-
fitting N-95 mask
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, grilling, and gasoline-powered lawn and garden
equipment

For the latest air quality forecasts and information, visit the
website at aqmd.gov.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

NWSheadline: AIR QUALITY ALERT FOR HARMFUL FINE PARTICLE POLLUTION LEVELS DUE TO WILDFIRE SMOKE

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 16 at 7:58PM CDT until October 20 at 4:00AM CDT by NWS Norman OK
properties.description:

Beaver Creek near Electra affecting Wilbarger and Wichita Counties.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Beaver Creek near Electra.

* WHEN...From Saturday evening to late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...At 26.0 feet, Flood levels up to 2 feet in depth cover
farm and range lands... and may inundate some oil and gas

properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 16 at 8:46PM EDT until October 17 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip
currents, large breaking waves expected, and strong longshore
currents in the surf zone. For the High Surf Advisory, large
breaking waves of 5 to 14 feet expected in the surf zone. For
the Coastal Flood Watch, up to one foot of inundation above
ground level possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and
tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Hatteras Island.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, from 8 AM EDT Saturday
through Saturday evening. For the High Surf Advisory, from 2
PM Saturday to 8 AM EDT Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch,
from Saturday afternoon through Tuesday morning.

* IMPACTS...2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level is
possible in some areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in an elevated threat of property damage. Flooding
will extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes
and businesses. Numerous road closures and flooding of vehicles
will be possible. Vulnerable portions of NC-12 may be inundated,
especially around high tide. Dangerous swimming and surfing
conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the
best swimmers away from shore into deeper water. Dangerous
shore break can throw a swimmer or surfer head first into the
bottom causing neck and back injuries. Strong longshore
currents will create dangerous swimming conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...This has the potential to be a long
duration event bringing more significant ocean overwash impacts
to vulnerable oceanside areas through multiple high tide cycles
into next week. Minor soundside water level rises will also be
possible.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, strong longshore
currents in the surf zone. For the Coastal Flood Watch, 2 to 4
feet of inundation above ground level possible in low-lying
areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf
Advisory, large breaking waves of 6 to 9 feet expected in the
surf zone.

* WHERE...Ocracoke Island.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, from 8 AM EDT Saturday
through Saturday evening. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from
Saturday afternoon through Tuesday morning. For the High Surf
Advisory, from midnight Saturday night to 8 PM EDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Up to 2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level is
possible in some areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in an elevated threat of property damage. Flooding
will extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes
and businesses. Numerous road closures and flooding of vehicles
will be possible. Vulnerable portions of NC-12 may be inundated,
especially around high tide. Dangerous swimming and surfing
conditions and localized beach erosion. Strong longshore
currents will create dangerous swimming conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...This has the potential to be a long
duration event bringing more significant ocean overwash impacts
to vulnerable oceanside areas through multiple high tide cycles
into next week. Minor soundside water level rises will also be
possible.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 16 at 8:46PM EDT until October 19 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, strong longshore
currents in the surf zone. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to
2 to 3 feet of inundation above ground level expected in low-
lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High
Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to 10 feet expected in
the surf zone.

* WHERE...East Carteret County.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, from 8 AM EDT Saturday
through Saturday evening. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from
5 PM Saturday to 8 PM EDT Monday. For the High Surf Advisory,
from midnight Saturday night to 8 PM EDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Up to 2 to 3 feet of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in a low threat of property damage. Some roads and low
lying property including parking lots, parks, lawns, and homes
adjacent to the waterfront will experience shallow flooding.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Strong longshore currents will create dangerous
swimming conditions.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Strong longshore currents can sweep swimmers and surfers into rip
currents, piers, jetties and other hazardous areas. In many
cases, the longshore current is strong enough to prevent swimmers
from being able to keep their feet on the bottom making it
difficult to return to shore.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 16 at 5:42PM PDT until October 17 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
...HIGH RISK FOR RAPID FIRE GROWTH AND EXTREME FIRE BEHAVIOR WITH
ANY NEW FIRE STARTS THROUGH SATURDAY, DUE TO MODERATE TO LOCALLY
STRONG SANTA ANA WINDS AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY...

Moderate to locally strong Santa Ana winds have peaked today then
will slowly weaken tonight through Saturday. The gusty offshore
winds combined with very warm and dry conditions will maintain
Red Flag Warnings for most of Los Angeles and Ventura Counties
through Saturday.

* AFFECTED AREA...Santa Clarita Valley, Ventura County Beaches,
Ventura County Inland Coast, Lake Casitas, Ojai Valley,
Central Ventura County Valleys, Malibu Coast, Calabasas and
Agoura Hills, Western San Fernando Valley, Eastern San
Fernando Valley, Southeastern Ventura County Valleys and Los
Angeles County San Gabriel Valley.

* TIMING...Until 8 PM PDT Saturday.

* WINDS...Northeast to east 20 to 35 mph with gusts of 40 to 50
mph tonight, lowering to 15 to 30 mph with gusts 30 to 45 mph
on Saturday.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Minimums of 8 to 15 percent common. Poor
overnight recoveries in the foothills and wind prone areas.

* IMPACTS...If fire ignition occurs, conditions are favorable
for extreme fire behavior which would threaten life and
property.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. Use extreme caution
with anything that can spark a wildfire. Residents near wildland
interfaces should be prepared to evacuate if a wildfire breaks
out. See readyforwildfire.org and wildfirerisk.org for
information.
